author: Barbara Conway Hala
text: It’s important to understand that CGMs read the glucose level in the interstitial fluid below the skin. It’s not the same as blood glucose and will often vary by about 30 points. It’s used to help you identify lows and highs that you should always confirm with a finger stick before treating. There’s a lag time between the interstitial glucose level and your blood glucose level. The CGM provides alarms and also a graph for the whole day so you can start to catch lows & highs before they become critical.
